question: Your extraction system processes 20,000 invoices per week and validates each output against a JSON schema. A verification pass then checks every extracted field against the source document. The human reviewers can check only a small share of the fields. How should you design the verification pass so that reviewer time goes to the fields most likely to be wrong?

options.text: Have the verification pass return one pass or fail verdict per document, and send every failed document to the human reviewers for a full manual check.
options.reason: A single verdict per document gives no confidence for each field, so the reviewers cannot focus on the fields most likely to be wrong.

options.text: Have the verification pass state how confident it is that each field value is correct, and route fields below a fixed 0.9 threshold to reviewers without any calibration.
options.reason: The guide calls for calibrating confidence scores against labeled validation sets, and an uncalibrated fixed threshold may not match the actual error rates.

options.text: Have the verification pass report its confidence that each field value is correct, calibrate the threshold on a labeled validation set, and route low-confidence fields to reviewers.
options.reason: Self-reported confidence for each finding enables calibrated review routing, and the guide calibrates confidence thresholds with labeled validation sets.

options.text: Have the same extraction session re-check its own output in a second pass, and route a field to the human reviewers only when the two passes disagree about the extracted value of that field.
options.reason: A session that keeps its generation reasoning context is less likely to question its own decisions, so it repeats its errors and gives no calibrated routing signal.
